description: LCD1602 through a PCF8574 I2C backpack at 0x27 (I2C1 PB6 SCL / PB7 SDA, 100 kHz): 4-bit init through the expander, text and an uptime counter updated every second
expect:
72 MHz. I2C1 PB6/PB7 AF open drain, 100 kHz standard mode (CCR 180); the backpack's 4.7 kOhm pull-ups go to its 5 V VCC (PB6/PB7 are 5 V tolerant). USART1 PA9/PA10 115200 8N1. Prints 'LCD1602 I2C demo
', waits 50 ms, probes 0x27 (2 trials): HAL_BUSY -> 'I2C bus busy: SDA/SCL stuck low (pull-ups?)
', no ACK (no backpack, a PCF8574A board at 0x3F) -> 'PCF8574 not found at 0x27 (no ACK)
', both stop. Port bits P0 = RS, P1 = RW (always 0), P2 = E, P3 = backlight (always 1), P4..P7 = D4..D7; every nibble is written twice (E high, E low). Init: port 08h, 50 ms, nibble 3h, 5 ms, 3h, 1 ms, 3h, 1 ms, 2h, then 28h, 0Ch, 01h, 2 ms, 06h; DDRAM 00h 'Hello via I2C!', 40h 'uptime'; prints 'LCD ready at 0x27
'. Every 1000 ms after that (deadline based) N = 1, 2, ... is written right-aligned in 6 digits at DDRAM 4Ah and 'uptime N s
' goes out on USART1. A failed transfer prints 'I2C error <HAL error code>
' and stops.

circuit: USART1: virtual terminal on PA9 (TX) / PA10 (RX)
no backpack on this bench: the probe of 0x27 is not acknowledged (the LCD contents are covered by tests/devices/displays-firmware.test.ts)

boot.USART1:
LCD1602 I2C demo
PCF8574 not found at 0x27 (no ACK)
